title: Smooth maps, the standard pathologies and the derivative
summary: Smooth maps and diffeomorphisms tested in charts (one atlas suffices); the line with two origins and the long line as witnesses that the Hausdorff and second countability axioms are independent of the atlas; distinct smooth structures on R that are diffeomorphic; Milnor's exotic spheres as a remark; the differential of a map between normed spaces and its uniqueness; rank, immersions and submersions.

objectives.description: Define smooth maps and diffeomorphisms between manifolds and prove that smoothness can be tested with one atlas on each side.
Construct the line with two origins, show it has a smooth atlas and is second countable but not Hausdorff, and derive the failure of unique limits.
Show that the charts x and x^3 on R give different smooth structures that are nonetheless diffeomorphic, and explain the distinction between structures and diffeomorphism classes.
State the definition of the differential, prove its uniqueness, and define rank, immersion and submersion with chart-independence justified.

preparation.description: Read lecture 2 of the 18.965 notes, page 1: §2 smooth maps and diffeomorphisms, §3 the line with two origins and the long line, Remark 1.
Read lecture 2 page 2: the long line is not second countable; 'Different charts' (R with x and x^3); Milnor's seven-sphere remark.
Read lecture 3: Definition 4.1 (the differential), the uniqueness argument, C^1 and higher derivatives, Definition 4.2 (immersion, submersion) and the linear models.
Read Hitchin §2.4 (maps between manifolds) for a second presentation of smooth maps and diffeomorphisms.

exitCheck.description: Exercise 1 accepted: the two-chart atlas verified with the identity transition map on R minus the origin, non-Hausdorffness proved via neighbourhoods of the two origins, the doubly convergent sequence exhibited and a compact non-closed set identified.

commonMisconceptions.claim: If the identity map between two smooth structures on the same space is smooth, the structures are the same.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Smoothness of the identity in one direction only shows one structure refines the other in a weak sense; the structures coincide only if the identity is a diffeomorphism. For (R, x) and (R, x^3) the identity is smooth one way, not the other, and the structures differ, yet the manifolds are diffeomorphic via a different map.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An injective immersion is an embedding, so its image is a submanifold.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The figure-eight curve is an injective immersion that is not a homeomorphism onto its image. Embeddings require the topological condition as well; see unit 3.

commonMisconceptions.claim: In a space with a smooth atlas, convergent sequences have unique limits.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Uniqueness of limits is a consequence of the Hausdorff axiom, not of the atlas: on the line with two origins the sequence 1/n converges to both origins.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The rank of a smooth map depends on the coordinates chosen.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Changing charts composes the chart expression with diffeomorphisms, whose differentials are invertible; the rank is unchanged by the chain rule.
